summary: 42links is a self-hosted bookmarking server designed to support multiple user accounts. It allows individuals or small groups to save, organise and retrieve web links from a centralised location. As a dedicated link-sharing tool, it operates in the same general domain as traditional read-later services and bookmark managers.
goodFor: It is suited for small user bases or individuals who want a self-hosted alternative for collaborative link storage rather than relying on commercial bookmarking platforms.
watchOut: The project has no tagged releases and minimal visible activity, meaning you may encounter rough edges, missing documentation, or lack of support. Additionally, its BSD-3-Clause-No-Military-License is a non-standard source licence that restricts military use, which may violate corporate compliance policies.
deployNotes: Because it is written in Common Lisp, you will typically need to run it behind a standard reverse proxy like Nginx or Caddy to handle TLS termination. You should also ensure persistent storage is configured for any underlying database or state it requires.
